newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sri Dhana Finance says no liquidity woes.
newsitem.headline: Sri Dhana Finance says no liquidity woes.

text.p: Thailand's Sri Dhana Finance and Securities said on Friday that it faced no liquidity problems and was not in need of help from the central bank.

The company said in a statement to the stock exchange that it was making the clarification following news reports that an unidentified finance company had suffered liquidity problems and the central bank had to help and order it to increase its capital.
"The company would like to report that it has increased capital for normal business expansion, which it regularly does," the firm said.
In 1996, the company had total assets of 21.23 billion baht ($816 million), a net profit of 124 million baht and retained earnings of 420 million.
"The company did not suffer liquidity problems and need help from the Bank of Thailand at all," it said.

On Thursday, the central bank denied that its governor Rerngchai Marakanond had said that a finance company was facing short-term liquidity problems. It added that no finance firms under its supervision faced liquidity problems.
